subject: bans
text:
- NEVER write any channel frame (`send`, `answer`, `hook.dialog`, `wait`/`last`, `pause`/`release`, `link`/`unlink`, and `hook.event` notifications, which carry prompt and reply text) before verifying the server's pid (Windows: the connected stream's peer pid, interprocess `peer_creds().pid()`, which calls `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the SQOS-adopted client end) or euid + pid (Linux/FreeBSD `peer_creds()`; the client-side euid check owed to the route entry "Unix endpoint and home hardening") plus sysinfo start time against `snapshot.json` (on macOS, where `peer_creds()` gives no pid: euid + the verified 0700 socket directory only, per the recorded known gap; the euid check is never skipped), and NEVER take those reference values (`endpoint`, `pid`, `started_at`) from a `snapshot.json` that has not passed the strict-modes check in the same process. The dated exceptions hold only the strict-modes half — the reference values taken from a `snapshot.json` read without the strict-modes check — owed to the Epoch 6 entry "Home and code-bearing file integrity"; on Linux and Windows each frame below verifies the serving process first (macOS: the recorded gap): `viola hook`'s `hook.event` (Decisions Log `2026-09-28`, ratified by the founder), CLI `viola send`'s `send` frame, CLI `viola wait` / `viola last`'s `wait` / `last` frames and CLI `viola answer`'s `answer` frame and CLI `viola pause` / `viola release`'s `pause` / `release` frames, each after the liveness pre-check and the server check, and `viola hook pre-tool-use|permission-request`'s `hook.dialog` frame after its payload shape check (the founder's rulings, live, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer; `answer` / `hook.dialog` the sixth dated gap; `pause` / `release` the seventh, F-W1), and `viola mcp`'s `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tool frames after the liveness pre-check and the server check (the eighth dated gap: the founder's own answer to P4 fork Q1, 2026-10-17, relayed by the overseer, `inputs#I2` of chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers); no other frame or process may borrow any of them.
 CLI `viola link` / `viola unlink`'s `link` / `unlink` frames meet this ban in full: they take `endpoint`, `pid` and `started_at` from a `snapshot.json` read after `check_instance` passed in the same process and verify the server through `cmd::client::connect` on Linux and Windows; only every client's euid check and macOS's pid and start-time check stay owed to "Unix endpoint and home hardening", and they borrow no dated exception.

subject: bans
origin: ## Security Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these) › ### Code Patterns
text: - NEVER let `run --mutants` wipe any directory except the Windows host mutation scratch `<repo parent>/viola-mutants-scratch`. A pure guard refuses (`scratch-refused`) unless the resolved path's final component is exactly `viola-mutants-scratch` and the repository is neither that directory nor inside it. A drive or filesystem root has no final component, so it is refused. A failed removal is `scratch-wipe-failed`. The wiped scratch is re-created owner-only through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir` (the protected user + SYSTEM DACL on Windows), so an instance tree a test lays inside it passes the strict-modes check as one under `%TEMP%` does; NEVER re-create it with a plain `create_dir_all`, whose inherited workspace-drive grants the check refuses, and NEVER loosen the check for it. NEVER fall back to `%TEMP%` or the repository, and NEVER print the path. The guard and the wipe run only on a Windows host (`HOST_SCRATCH = cfg!(windows)`); elsewhere the harness touches no scratch, and the Linux dev host's same-named NOCOW `TMPDIR` for mutation runs is the operator's, never wiped by the harness.

subject: bans
origin: ## Security Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these) › ### Code Patterns
text: - NEVER let a test-side removal under `target/e2e-home` take anything but a dir the test side itself created: the root fixture chain's owner sweep and a test home's drop (by `owner.json` record, by its own `TempDir`) and harness `cleanup` (by the `viola-session-` name). On the Linux dev host that path is a link to the per-user tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>`, so these creations and removals reach outside the working directory: a boundary widening, ratified by the founder (live, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, after it was shown to him as creating and deleting outside the working directory through the link; relayed by the overseer). The two keepers (`prepare_home_base` in `tests/support/home.rs`, `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` in the harness) NEVER follow a linked base unless its target is absolute and one `lstat` of it reads a real directory with no group or other bit; a target that is itself a link is refused, so is a backing whose filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), and a refusal is a fixed message that names no path (the headroom one holds the two counts). They create the target with mode 0700 through the directory builder (never a chmod after, never a parent) and remove nothing. Ownership is not read separately: the `tempdir_in` that follows succeeds in an owner-only directory only for its owner. `viola` itself never reads or writes the backing by that name, and no CI runner has the link.

subject: bans
text:
- NEVER answer a `hook.dialog` with a non-`null` decision unless `ledger/stamps.json` holds a `viola verify` stamp for the child's CLI version. NEVER let any process other than `viola verify` write `ledger/stamps.json`. A stamp is what switches on dialog answering, including PermissionRequest `allow` (Threat Model Sec 1 config; architecture.md CLI Version Compatibility).
 The ledger has twenty-four rows (`LedgerRow::ALL`: the six spine rows, the four screen and timing rows, the four dialog-tier rows `question-answer` · `plan-approve-revise` · `question-notes` · `dialog-concurrency`, the three framing rows `long-paste-wrapper` · `tag-escaping` · `local-command-clear`, the newline row `paste-newline`, the three statusline rows `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` · `statusline-rate-limits`, the resume row `resume-session`, the agents row `agents-join` and the compact row `local-command-compact`), and a stamp is read over the relied set (`LedgerRow::relied()`, counter `/24` on Unix; on Windows, where the status line is not wrapped, the first eighteen, `resume-session`, `agents-join` and `local-command-compact`, counter `/21`), so a non-`null` decision flows only when every relied row passes: a home stamped `20 pass  4 fail` on Unix (`17 pass  4 fail` on Windows) records `cli_verified:false`, and so does a stamp holding exactly the fourteen older ids, or exactly the seventeen of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row, all `pass`, and, on every OS, one holding exactly the eighteen of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows or exactly the twenty-one of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows, or exactly the twenty-two of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, or exactly the twenty-three of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row; the hook prints nothing and `answer` exits 12 `unverified-cli`. The dated gap (R2, the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-04) under which decisions flowed on the ten-row stamp is closed.

subject: bans
text: - NEVER let `config.json`, a `VIOLA_*` environment variable or a CLI flag switch off any control in this plan: the IPC DACL or socket-directory check, the peer or server verification, the home strict-modes check or `validate_paste_text`. Environment variables are not a configuration channel (architecture.md Cross-cutting Patterns: Config management), and `VIOLA_DIR` is set by a child any same-session agent can influence. The two carve-outs are the test seams `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` (capped at 5 s; Decisions Log 2026-09-27) and `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` (fires only on the exact value `1`, a forced fail-open `hook` panic; Decisions Log 2026-09-28): each exists only under `cfg(feature = "fake-agent")`, is absent from every release build and switches off nothing (§Input Validation). The terminal colour facts `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM` are read in every build (the founder's own word, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline), only by `viola list`'s human mode and only to choose whether and how deep SGR bytes are written: they switch off no control (no escaping, no `validate_paste_text`, no check), widen no redaction and are not a configuration channel (§Input Validation). NEVER add another such seam or environment read, let these reach a release build, or let a colour fact change a control or reach a log line, error or refusal, without its own Decisions Log entry.
